title: "Quiz: sequences and pixels"

[Exercises](22-data-representations.qmd) · [Weekly revision](quiz.qmd)

Try each question before opening its hint or answer.

---

**Q1.** Predict these results:

```r
dna <- "ACGT"
length(dna)
nchar(dna)
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Count stored strings separately from characters within a string.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
`length(dna)` is 1; `nchar(dna)` is 4.
:::

---

**Q2.** An invented sequence contains A11, C9, G9 and T11. Its first A is replaced by G in a new object. What are its length and GC fraction, defined as `(G + C) / total letters`?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Replacement changes a label without inserting or deleting a position.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The length stays 40. The new counts are A10, C9, G10 and T11, so GC fraction is `19 / 40 = 0.475`. The original was `18 / 40 = 0.45`.
:::

---

**Q3.** A matrix contains 40 pixels at intensity 25 and 24 at intensity 210. What do these give?

```r
sum(pixels > 210)
sum(pixels >= 210)
mean(pixels > 100)
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
`>` excludes equality; `>=` includes it. In a numeric calculation, `TRUE` counts as 1.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The results are 0, 24 and `24 / 64 = 0.375`.
:::

---

**Q4.** Add 30 to every intensity in that matrix. How many pixels are now above 220? Does the change establish that the pictured object became physically larger?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The two intensity levels become 55 and 240; the positions stay fixed.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
24 pixels are above 220, compared with zero before the shift. This reflects brightness crossing a threshold. Physical area needs calibration and a justified definition of the object.
:::

---

**Q5.** A plant image contains 64 pixels. Which statement is supported?

(i) There are 64 independently treated plants.

(ii) There are 64 measured image positions.

(iii) The bright area must be one cell.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Ask what one matrix cell represents.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(ii). Pixels are image positions. They do not supply independent plant treatment allocation or establish a cell’s identity.
:::
